title: Security Deposit Assessment: Triggers, Timing and Required Amount
content:
**Rule on assessment of a Security Deposit.**

**1. Triggers.** A Security Deposit is assessed only for one of the triggers its kind carries:
(a) a new service agreement opened without a waiver basis;
(b) a disconnection of the agreement for nonpayment;
(c) late payment charges on the agreement in the 12 months before assessment reaching the kind's late payment trigger count, counted as the late payment charges posted on the agreement in the 12 calendar months ending on the assessment date, excluding charges waived by a courtesy late-charge waiver credit;
(d) a confirmed finding of meter tampering or diversion.

**2. Kind.** The deposit kind follows the customer class and the agreement's rate schedule as listed for each kind.

**3. New-service timing.** A new-service deposit must be assessed within the assessment window after the agreement's start date.

**4. Counting.** Each window is counted in calendar days from the day after its triggering date, and an assessment on the last day of the window is in time.

**5. Disconnection date.** The disconnection date is the agreement's last status date while it is disconnected.

**6. Reconnection and energization.** Where the kind requires the first installment before reconnection, a disconnected agreement is not reconnected until the first installment is received; where the kind requires the deposit to be fully secured before energization, a new agreement is not energized until the deposit is held.

**7. Evidence.** Each timing test reads the system record of the triggering date, the agreement's start date, its last status date, the posting date of the late payment charge, or the date of the field investigation, for the agreement, charge or field order concerned, as the records show it before the deposit is assessed.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of this rule are no longer in force and are superseded by the current basis:

- A deposit triggered by disconnection must be assessed within the assessment window after the disconnection date. (no longer in force)
- A deposit triggered by late payments must be assessed within the assessment window after the posting date of the late payment charge that reached the trigger count. (no longer in force)
- A deposit triggered by unauthorized use must be assessed within the assessment window after the date of the field investigation that confirmed it. (no longer in force)
- The required amount is the kind's multiple times the average monthly bill, rounded up to the next whole dollar, then raised to the kind's minimum deposit and limited to its maximum deposit; the average monthly bill being the mean, rounded to the cent, of the kind's number of most recent regular bills of the agreement before the assessment date, or the kind's default average bill when the agreement has fewer regular bills than the kind requires. (no longer in force)
- The installment count is the kind's most installments, or its most installments when income-qualified where the customer's income qualification runs to or past the assessment date, reduced until each installment reaches the kind's smallest installment. (no longer in force)
- The first installment is due the kind's first-installment days after assessment and later installments under the kind's installment schedule. (no longer in force)

## Boundary cases for the new-service window (hypothetical dates)

For a kind with a 30-day assessment window and an agreement start date of 10 April, the first counted day is 11 April and the last day of the window is 10 May.

| Assessment date | In time? |
|---|---|
| 9 May | Yes |
| 10 May (last day of the window) | Yes |
| 11 May | No |

Expressed generally: an assessment on the last calendar day of the window is in time, and an assessment on the following day is not.

## Points of judgement

- A trigger the kind does not carry does not support an assessment of that kind.
- A late payment charge that was waived by a courtesy late-charge waiver credit does not count toward the late payment trigger count.
